{{Quote|Mandalorian Space was occupied and disarmed, with a caretaker government created from elements of the failed peace movement. The occupation would last for decades, and create a new schism in Mandalorian society.|Vilnau Teupt|<ref name="Warfare" />}}
The '''Mandalorian Excision''' of [[738 BBY]]&mdash;known to [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] natives as the '''''Dral'Han''''', or the '''Annihilation'''&mdash;was a brief but brutal conflict that saw the devastation of [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian Space]] at the hands of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Following the Republic's enactment of the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]] in [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the Mandalorian people experienced a growth in technological prowess and military power, but they refused to join the Republic due to their traditional warrior ways. Alarmed by the rising threat of the Mandalorians, the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] organized the Republic's [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] and [[Planetary Security Forces]] in a preemptive strike on Mandalorian [[Realspace/Legends|Space]]. The Mandalorians had no hope of winning a war against the Republic and suffered greatly in the resulting battles, with a number of [[Planet/Legends|planets]] including [[Fenel]], [[Ordo/Legends|Ordo]], [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]], and [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] itself crippled by bombardment. The damage lasted for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], with entire sections of Mandalorian worlds remaining barren [[Desert/Legends|deserts]].

Following the Excision, the Republic disarmed and occupied Mandalorian Space, installing a provisional government to oversee [[Sector/Legends|sectoral]] affairs. The Mandalorians preserved their distinctive culture, as well as their resentment of the Republic and the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who had defeated them, while rebuilding the worlds that the war had left scarred. The Excision led to the formation of the pacifistic [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]], who prevailed over the warrior clans in many areas of governmental operation and society, becoming the new rulers of Mandalore. Nevertheless, many unrepentant warriors continued their traditional practices, eventually leading to the formation of such splinter groups as the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]. The schism in ideology ensured that [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|further]] [[Great Clan Wars/Legends|conflict]] would ensue, as it did well into the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Background==
{{Quote|[Some clan leaders] argued that Mandalore should join the Republic, immediately becoming one of its most powerful and influential sectors. But the peacemakers were shouted down: If Mandalorians weren't warriors, they weren't Mandalorians at all.|Vilnau Teupt|<ref name="Warfare" />}}
[[File:Mandalorians_-_TEA.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Mandalorian warrior clans long nursed a hatred of the Republic and the Jedi Order.]]
In the last [[Time/Legends|millennia]] of the regime of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warrior people of [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian Space]] clashed with the Republic on numerous occasions, most notably in the [[Mandalorian Wars]] from [[3976 BBY]] to [[3960 BBY]]. After [[Battle of Malachor V|losing]] their [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|leader]], [[Mandalore the Ultimate]], the Mandalorian warrior clans were disarmed and surrendered to the Republic, though they were left with a simmering resentment of the Republic and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] that had defeated them. The Mandalorian [[Canons of Honor|warrior codes]] came to be followed only in Mandalorian [[Realspace/Legends|Space]], but it was not until the emergence of a new leader, [[Mandalore the Uniter]], in [[1051 BBY]] that the Mandalorians began to reclaim stability in their lawless area of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. In a movement known as the [[Return (Mandalorian)|Return]], Mandalore the Uniter urged his fragmented people to strengthen and defend Mandalorian Space. They were thus able to survive the millennium-long [[New Sith Wars]] and grew to be a regional industrial power, safeguarding neighboring [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] and [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] from trouble<ref name="Warfare" /> while also advancing in technology and military strength. It was during this time that Mandalorian Space, primarily the Mandalorian [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], reached an apex in its military power.<ref name="TEA" />

As Mandalorian Space returned to [[Galaxy/Legends|galactic]] prominence<ref name="Warfare" /> as a rigidly disciplined society,<ref name="TEA" /> the Republic, left weakened and splintered after the New [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Wars, began to draw itself back together following the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformations]] of [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. The Republic's re-institutionalization of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] thus reopened conflict with Mandalorian Space. Although first seen as a much-needed source of stability, the Mandalorians&mdash;who had begun to tax commerce along the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], were forcing economic and defense pacts onto bordering sectors, and disregarded the Republic's new defense force restrictions altogether&mdash;re-emerged as a threat to the Republic. Some pro-peace clan leaders believed that Mandalorian Space should join the Republic as one of its most powerful and influential sectors, as they had no chance of winning a direct engagement with the Republic. Nevertheless, the Mandalorians' overall position was resoundingly for continued independence, as popular opinion held that non-warrior Mandalorians could not claim to be Mandalorians at all. That mindset prevailed for several [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], until the Republic and the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Order decided to move preemptively against the ever-resistant Mandalorians.<ref name="Warfare" />

==The Excision==
{{Quote|The Mandalorian Excision was brief but overwhelming: Key Mandalorian worlds such as Fenel, Ordo, Concord Dawn, and Mandalore itself were subjected to devastating bombardment, with swaths of those worlds still desolate in Imperial times.|Vilnau Teupt|<ref name="Warfare" />}}
[[File:Sundari_Desert.png|thumb|right|250px|Key worlds such as Mandalore were exposed to fierce Republic bombardment.]]
In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[738 BBY]], the Republic authorized the creation of a task force to remove the threat of the Mandalorians as an opposing power. The Republic's [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]] were called in alongside units from various [[Planetary Security Forces]] of the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]], with members of the Jedi Order serving as [[Commander/Legends|commanders]] for the war effort.<ref name="Warfare" /> The Jedi led their [[Troop/Legends|troops]] to Mandalorian Space,<ref name="TEA" /> striking at key Mandalorian worlds such as [[Fenel]], [[Ordo/Legends|Ordo]], and [[Concord Dawn/Legends|Concord Dawn]], as well as Mandalore itself. In the battles that followed,<ref name="Warfare" /> Republic [[Warship/Legends|warships]]<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref> exposed the targeted [[Planet/Legends|planets]] of Mandalorian Space to devastating bombardment,<ref name="Warfare" /> creating barren [[Desert/Legends|deserts]] of [[Color/Legends|white]] sand from entire regions of the planetary surfaces,<ref name="TCW New Battlefronts" /> including [[Tree/Legends|forests]] and [[Farm/Legends|farmland]].<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" /> Having lacked from the start any hope of repelling a Republic attack,<ref name="Warfare" /> the Mandalorian clans were defeated,<ref name="Visual Guide Updated" /> and the Jedi&ndash;Republic forces claimed victory.<ref name="Warfare" /> Many Mandalorian warriors were [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]], disarmed, or killed as a result of the conflict.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />

==Aftermath==
===A schism in ideals===
{{Quote|The Republic called this dishonorable assault the Mandalorian Excision, as if we were cancerous tissue to be cut out of the galaxy. We call it the Dral'Han&mdash;the Annihilation.|Tor Vizsla|<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />}}
[[File:New_Mandalorians.png|thumb|left|250px|The New Mandalorians emerged following the Excision, espousing peace to save their world.]]
The Mandalorian Excision, the Republic's name for the short but brutal war, left Mandalorian Space crippled. Mandalorian natives remembered the conflict as the ''Dral'Han'', translated from [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] as "the Annihilation."<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" /> In a move that would last for [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]], the Republic occupied and disarmed Mandalorian Space, establishing a loyal caretaker government for the sector from remnants of the pro-Republic peace movement from before the war. The occupation of Mandalore birthed a schism in ideology within Mandalorian society: In opposition to the warrior clans rose the pacifistic [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]] from the caretaker government. Resenting the Republic but seeing no benefit to continued opposition, the New Mandalorians renounced the ages-old warrior codes for nonviolence and neutrality<ref name="Warfare" /> in an effort to save their ravaged homeworld.<ref name="TEA" />

The New Mandalorians triumphed over the warrior clans, holding most positions of power and gaining rule of Mandalorian Space,<ref name="Warfare" /> due to the fact that the majority of Mandalorians were weary of war. Nevertheless, the societal rift in ideology shaped the following centuries of Mandalorian history. Those who continued to practice the outlawed [[Resol'nare|warrior ways]] in secret became known as the [[Aka'liit|Faithful]], while the New Mandalorians were termed the Faithless. None of the Mandalorian clans escaped the enduring divisions between the so-called Faithful and Faithless.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />

The devastation to Mandalore and other worlds lasted far beyond the Excision, with the desolation in many areas remaining well into the time of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Warfare" /> In spite of the scars to their homes, the Mandalorians retained their distinctive culture and style of technology.<ref name="TCW Incredible Vehicles">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]''</ref> Since the white sand deserts of Mandalore were uninhabitable, the New Mandalorians who remade their world engineered massive<ref name="TCW New Battlefronts" /> [[Bio-cube/Legends|bio-cube]]<ref name="Dataclip: The Mandalore Plot">{{CN|url=tv_shows/starwars/?episodeID=8a250596267a117c01267bec7d380004|text=Dataclip: The Mandalore Plot|na=video file}}</ref> [[City/Legends|cities]] as part of their new civilization.<ref name="TCW New Battlefronts" /> Their [[Domed city/Legends|domed]] [[Capital/Legends|capital]], [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]], was one such city that was erected amidst the inhospitable sands.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot">{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}}</ref>

For the Republic, the Excision brought into question the best methods for coordinating various units of the Planetary Security Forces, an endeavor that the Republic's war effort had necessitated. Following the Excision, various Republic marshals and [[Admiral/Legends|admirals]] met at the [[Corsin Retreat]] to deliberate on the subject, leading to the revival of the Republic [[Navy/Legends|Naval]] College as the [[Republic Navy War College/Legends|College of Planetary Security Forces]] on [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]].<ref name="Warfare" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Mandalore's ''violent past'' is behind us. All of our warriors were exiled to our moon, Concordia. They died out ''years'' ago.|[[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]] [[Almec/Legends|Almec]] of the New Mandalorians|<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" />}}
[[File:BoKatanNightOwls-AFIN.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Divisions among the Mandalorian Faithful led to the creation of factions like the Death Watch.]]
As Mandalore was rebuilt as an industrial power over the next few centuries, a number of unrepentant warriors and [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] were [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]].<ref name="Warfare" /> Others kept to the regions of Mandalore that were unspoiled by war like the traditional capital of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]],<ref name="Order 66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref><ref name="True Colors">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref> or ventured out into the galaxy to become [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] like their ancestors.<ref name="Warfare" /> The following generations of the Faithful soon encountered further divisions,<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" /> with a [[Supercommando Codex|reformist]] movement known as the [[True Mandalorians]] coming into conflict with the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]], a splinter group of [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] radicals, in [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]]. The ensuing [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]] ended with the [[Battle of Galidraan|decimation]] of the True Mandalorians in [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]], while the Death Watch survived<ref name="Warfare" /> and later initiated an attempt to overthrow the New Mandalorians. The result was the [[Great Clan Wars/Legends|Great Clan Wars]],<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy">''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]''</ref> a [[Blood/Legends|bloody]] civil war that killed a great number of Mandalorians<ref name="Voyage of Temptation">{{TCW|Voyage of Temptation}}</ref> and exacerbated the devastation to Mandalore that the Excision had originally wrought.<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> Though defeated, the Death Watch [[Secret Mandalore|leader]] [[Tor Vizsla]] survived the upheaval, and he wrote about the Annihilation in his Death Watch manifesto ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]''.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />

The New Mandalorians remained in power following the Great Clan Wars, much to the chagrin of the Death Watch,<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> which allied itself with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] of [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] to 19 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]]. In doing so, the Death Watch hoped to finally overthrow the New Mandalorians and exact revenge upon the Republic for its savagery during the Excision.<ref name="Warfare" /> By that time, the New Mandalorians won [[Senator/Legends|representation]] in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] for<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> the so-called "New Mandalore."<ref name="UK Comic 6.20">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.20|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.20]]</ref> The neutrality of Mandalore continued from the post-Excision era<ref name="Warfare" /> well into the Clone Wars thanks to the efforts of [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], who emerged as the [[Anti-Mandalore|leader]] of the New Mandalorians at that time. In spite of [[Plot to assassinate Satine Kryze/Legends|hindrances]] by the Death Watch and the Confederacy, Kryze was able to [[Mandalore Defense Resolution/Legends|preserve]] the [[Politics/Legends|political]] isolation of the [[Mandalore system/Legends|Mandalore system]] in the war while remaining loyal to the Republic.<ref name="Duchess of Mandalore">{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}}</ref>

Yet, the warrior ways ultimately won out over pacifism, with both the Death Watch and New Mandalorians suffering critical losses from further infighting,<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> and the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]] rising to power under the leadership of a new Mandalore, [[Spar]].<ref name="TEA" /> Decades later, the Mandalorian Excision was one of the chapters of Mandalorian history that the [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Vilnau Teupt]] documented in his [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]] [[Industry, Honor, Savagery: Shaping the Mandalorian Soul|keynote address]] at the [[Brentaal Academy]].<ref name="Warfare" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|We get more detail about the conflict between the Republic and Jedi and the Mandalorians&mdash;a conflict I called the Mandalorian Excision. I wanted a cold, clinical name&mdash;one that clearly expressed the Republic's attitude about Mandalore, and that would ensure Mandalorian hatred and resentment. I also wanted to show where the New Mandalorians came from&mdash;that their roots were in an effort to engage with the Republic (though on Mandalorian terms) and avoid war.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Warfare Endnotes Pt. 4">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/21728447315/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-4|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 4}}</ref>}}
[[File:Mandalore-TEA.png|thumb|left|200px|The retconned Mandalore, ravaged by the Mandalorian Excision]]
The Mandalorian Excision,<ref name="Warfare" /> created as a backstory for a [[2010]] [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]] story arc of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series,<ref name="The Complete Season Two">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]], "Creating Mandalore" Featurette</ref> represented a [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] in the history of the planet Mandalore in the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]]. Mandalore was a prominent location in author [[Karen Traviss]]'s [[Republic Commando|''Republic Commando'' novel series]] from [[2007]] on, which portrayed it as a more arboreal world.<ref name="True Colors" /> When the Mandalorians were to be explored in the ''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' television series, the backstory for Mandalore&mdash;created by crew members such as Series Supervising Director [[Dave Filoni]] with input from Series Producer [[George Lucas]]&mdash;was that the world had been devastated to the point that its surface had been laid to waste. That destruction had led to the formation of the pacifistic New Mandalorians, who were featured as part of the second season storyline.<ref name="The Complete Season Two" />

Beginning in [[August]] [[2009]] with ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', reference material reflected the change in [[canon]]. ''The Essential Atlas'' introduced a conflict between the Mandalorians and the Jedi as the reason for the devastated Mandalore,<ref name="TEA" /> whose barren surface was portrayed in the series.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" /> Co-authors [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]] did not learn about the series' retcon of Mandalore until they were almost finished with ''The Essential Atlas'', so Fry worked quickly with [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and [[Leland Chee]] of [[Lucasfilm]] to integrate the new information, particularly with the Jedi&ndash;Mandalorian conflict.<ref name="Warfare Endnotes Pt. 4" /> Fry was later able to explore the details of the event in ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'', published in [[April]] [[2012]]. He named the event the "Mandalorian Excision"<ref name="Warfare" /> as a clear message of the Republic's cold treatment of Mandalore to ensure Mandalorian resentment.<ref name="Warfare Endnotes Pt. 4" />

''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', released in [[2013]], was the first publication to visually depict the Excision. It also went into further detail about the event's aftermath and legacy via an [[in-universe]] narrative allegedly authored by Tor Vizsla. However, the artwork depicts<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" /> a [[Fury-class Imperial interceptor|''Fury''-class Imperial interceptor]] of the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]] and a Republic [[Valor-class cruiser|''Valor''-class cruiser]], both of which originate in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' that is set [[3640 BBY|3000 years prior]]<ref name="TOR-Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref> to the Excision.<ref name="Warfare" />
